
###A) Basic Review###

Write four input statements to store the following:

* my_name (Ask the user for their name)

* my_age (Ask the user for the age)

* my_grade (Ask the user for their grade [as a word, not as a number])

* my\_fav\_color (Ask the user for their favorite color)

Use that information to print a statement like this one:

<h4>"My name is <u>Sonny</u>, and my favorite color is <u>blue</u>. I am <u>15</u> years old and a <u>Sophomore.</u>"</h4>


   
###B) Some Math###
Write two input statements to store the following:

* radius (Ask the user to enter a circle's radius)
* height (Ask the user to enter a cylinder's height)

![A figure that shows the area of a right cylinder. In red is a circle on the top of the cylinder. The rest of the cylinder is extruded underneath that circle, with the height marked "h". There is a right angle shown between the radius of the circle and the height of the cylinder. Above the figure is the formula v = base * h, with "base" in the same red color as the circle.](data:image/png;base64,)

Calculate the area of the base of the circle using the formula A = πr². ![A figure labelled "Area of Circle". It features a grey circle with black outline and text. The formula Area equals pi r squared is above the center of the circle. A dotted radius labelled "r" procedes from the center of the circle to the bottom.](https://www.onlinemathlearning.com/image-files/area-circle.png)  
Then, multiply that by the height of the cylinder to find the volume.  
<p></p>

  
Use that information to print a statement like this one:
<p></p>
<h4>"If a cylinder has a radius of <u>7.5</u>, and and a height of  <u>10</u>, it would have a base area of <u>176.625</u> square units and a volume of <u>1766.25</u> cubic units."</h4>
